Soil is non-coherent (single grain structure) and it breaks under very gentle pressure, i.e., Sandy soils.
Weakly resistant to pressure and soil materials breaks easily under gentle to moderate pressure i.e., sandy loam / loam
Very resistant to pressure and soil materials is not easily broken between the thumbs and fore finger, i.e., Clay loam and clay
Water removed from the soil readily/instantly, but not rapidly. Well drained soils commonly retain optimum amounts of moisture for plant growth after rain or application of irrigation water.

Water removed from the soil rather slowly, so that the profile is wet for a short but significant length of time. Moderately well drained soils commonly have slowly permeable layer or relatively high water table at a depth of 1 meter in the rainy season.

Water removed from the soil slowly. The soil remains intermittently wet in the rainy season but flood water will not remain on the surface for more than 15 days continuously. The ground water table remains within 1 meter from the surface for a certain period of time in the rainy season.
Water removed from the soil so slowly that soil remains flooded from 15 days to few months. The land may even remain wet after the rainy season.
The soil remains submerged under water for more than 8 months in a year and it remains wet almost throughout the year.

Plant available soil moisture content lasts for one to two months
Plant available soil moisture content lasts for two to three months
Plant available soil moisture content lasts for more than three months
Surface water drains out from soil by Mid-September to Mid-October (between 15 September to 14 October).
Surface water drains out from soil between Mid-October to Mid-November (15 October to 14 November).
Surface water drains out from soil between Mid-November to Mid-December (15 November to 14 December).
Surface water drains out from soil between Mid-December to end December (15 December to 30 December).
Surface water drains out from soil after December (after 30 December).
